plugins.//: The sentence iOS shows in the permission dialog. It has to say what the app does with the photos, not that it would like some: a vague one is a refusal and, at review, a rejection.
plugins.photosPermission: SparkTower uses your photos so you can add them to posts, updates and your profile.
plugins.//2: The camera is not asked for: nothing in the app takes a picture, and an unused permission string is a question at review with no good answer.

plugins.//: The launch screen. Until SDK 57 this was the top-level `splash` key; nothing reads that any more, so a build made from it opened to a blank white screen — the first thing a store reviewer would have seen.
plugins.//2: The tower, not splash-icon.png: that file is the placeholder Expo ships with a new project — grey concentric circles on a grid — and it was still what this app opened on. The mark is white, so it needs a ground with some colour in it; brand purple in light, black in dark.

dark.//: Otherwise a phone in dark mode opens on a full white screen and then drops to black when the app paints — the first half-second of every launch, and the jarring kind.

plugins.//: The notification icon on Android. Android draws it as a silhouette — every non-transparent pixel becomes white — so a full-colour logo arrives as a white square. The mark is a single shape and survives that; anything with detail would not.
plugins.//2: The colour behind the icon in the status bar. Brand purple, so a notification is recognisable at a glance before it is read.
plugins.//3: No `sounds`: the default is what people expect from an app that tells them somebody replied, and a custom sound is a decision to make deliberately rather than by shipping a file.

plugins.//: Saving a picture Nova drew to the camera roll. Only the *add* permission: the app never reads somebody's photo library through this — choosing a photo to upload is expo-image-picker, which asks for its own and says so.
plugins.savePhotosPermission: SparkTower saves the logos and images Nova makes for you to your photos, so you can use them anywhere.
plugins.//2: `photosPermission` is deliberately false. Asking to *read* the library would be a second dialog for something this does not do, and an unused permission is a question at review with no good answer.
plugins.//3: And no `isAccessMediaLocationEnabled`: the GPS coordinates inside somebody's photos are not this app's business.

extra.//: Production API. Every build profile in eas.json also sets EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL explicitly, which wins over this; this value is the safe default if it is ever missing. Local development points at localhost through mobile/.env (see .env.example).
extra.//newArch: The New Architecture is the default from SDK 53 on, and `newArchEnabled` was removed from the config schema — leaving it set made `expo-doctor` fail its schema check on every run, which is the check that tells you a build is going to behave unexpectedly. Removing it changes nothing: it was set to true, which is what happens anyway.
